lead: Christoffer Sehested, Vienna, to Frederik III and chancellor Christen Thomesen Sehested, Jan-May 1657 (row 5 of research/sweep_2026-11-11_nordic/candidates.json)
shelfmark: Rigsarkivet, TKUA, Speciel del, Kejseren: Gesandtskabsrelationer med bilag, 1630-58, laeg 'Relationer fra Christoffer Sehested 1657' (Fridericia: Oestrig 46; Gigas: Geh. Ark., Oesterrig 46 b)
scan: Arkivalieronline epid 19852211, unit 260651; images 108-172 all downloaded at full size on 11 Nov 2026 and viewed (64 frames); crops read at full size: 109, 112, 114, 116, 118, 124, 132, 138, 157, 169
verdict_reason: Not an open cipher. (1) The system is a monoalphabetic number substitution with a t-shaped word divider and about twenty nomenclator signs: it reads on sight (image 132 gives letter values between the lines: 32=w 15=i 13=o 2=l 17=c 7=h 72=n 48=t 5=e 80=r 96=s 9=d 26=u/v 6=a 25=m 40=g 12=z 4=b 30=f; with these, image 118 opens 'weiln ich E.K.M. bereits zu unterschiedenen mahlen von meiner hiesigen verrichtung ausfuhrlige ... nachricht ertheilet'). (2) The Danish chancery deciphered it in 1657: plaintext leaves and interlinear decipherments are in the volume, and they resolve the signs (margin and interline of image 132: XX = alliance, a sign = Conde de Rebolledo, another = K.M., X glossed with a name of a prince). (3) E. Gigas read the letters and quotes them in German in Grev Bernardino de Rebolledo (1883), pp. 282-284 notes ('Sehesteds Cifferbreve til Fred. III og den kgl. Kantsler af 27 Jan. n. St.'; quotes 'die Gemuether alhie nicht wenig ermunteret' from the letters of 17 Feb to the king and 24 Feb to the chancellor; cites letters to the chancellor of 15 Apr, 2 May, 19 May and to Gersdorf of 5 May); Fridericia (1894, note 62) used Gigas's decipherment. No full text of the letters is printed in either book.

letters.decipherment: this IS a decipherment; its cipher original was not identified among images 108-172 (it is neither 116-117 nor 118-119, whose openings were read and differ)

without_decipherment_in_volume: Most of the corpus: the king's letters of 17/27 Jan, 7/17 Feb and 14/24 Feb, the chancellor's letters of 14/24 Feb (first three pages), about 18/28 Feb and 21 Feb/3 Mar, and the cipher passages of March-May 1657. Deciphered in the volume: chancellor 17/27 Jan (112-113), one further letter to the king of late January (114-115), chancellor 7/17 Feb (19th-century slips 124-125), and interlinear parts of images 132, 138, 140.
gigas: Opened: E. Gigas, Grev Bernardino de Rebolledo, spansk Gesandt i Kjoebenhavn 1648-1659 (1883), archive.org grevbernardinode00giga full text, pp. 282-284 and 289 notes. Gigas cites and quotes the cipher letters from the manuscript; he prints no decipherment. Whether his full decipherment survives (the 19th-century slips in the volume are probably his or the archive's) was not determined.
use: Reference material and an easy transcription target (plaintext unpublished), not a catalogue entry: suggest closing the lead with verdict 'read' (trivial monoalphabetic cipher, read by the chancery in 1657 and by Gigas in 1883). It is a good small corpus for a 'known system, unpublished text' write-up if wanted.
